3.0.0.en: Knoweth us: that is, accepts our conduct.

3.0.1.en: Knew him: that is, believes in Him.

3.0.2.en: The Apostle boasts of the grace of God that has granted us sonship to Him. It is love and great condescension on His part to call us His children, and this sonship means many things. It gives us the right to draw near to Him, to enjoy His company and His protection of us... and more than this, to be with Him forever in eternity. That the evil world does not accept our pure conduct is not strange, because it did not believe in God our Father and therefore does not know or accept His children.

3.1.0.en: St. John rises from the blessings of sonship that we partly enjoy here on earth to a level of greatness and exaltation that we cannot comprehend, which is our sonship and communion with God in eternity. But here he states an important truth about eternity, which is that, as long as we are His children, we shall be like Him in luminosity. That is, by His fatherhood He grants us to live at a high level of spirituality, glory and radiance, as much as we can bear; He is unlimited, and He gives us what suits us according to our limitedness.

3.2.0.en: One of the effects of our faith and of our holding fast to our sonship to God is that we reject sin and live in purity like our pure and holy heavenly Father.

3.3.0.en: The reason for our rejecting sin and holding to a life of purity is that sin is a transgression of God's commandments. Because we are His children, our sonship to Him cannot agree with transgressing against God and His word, so we reject every sin and keep far from it whenever we remember that we are children of God.

3.4.0.en: Here he affirms that Christ, who appeared in the flesh to take away our sins by His death for us, is pure, that is, without sin, and because we are His children we live in purity.

3.5.0.en: Abiding in our sonship to God makes us averse to sin because it is against His word, and because we love Him we do not accept what angers Him and cannot disobey Him. But whoever accepts sin has in effect given up his sonship to God and is not abiding in Him, and whoever persists in sin shows that he has not known God, for how can he enjoy the sonship of God and then easily accept giving it up in order to sin?

3.6.0.en: Here he also states that doing righteousness is a grace given to the children of God, because God their Father is righteous, so their sonship to Him naturally drives them to do righteousness.

3.7.0.en: On the other hand, sin and transgression against God have their origin in the devil, and whoever commits them declares his sonship to him. Christ became incarnate to restore people to sonship to Him and to draw them out of the hand of the devil, so that they live in righteousness.

3.8.0.en: Therefore whoever is born of God lives in righteousness, and his sonship makes him averse to sin, because the new nature that God gave him in Baptism and planted in him makes him inclined to be like God and to abide in his sonship, and keeps him away from sin, so that he cannot bear to be in it.

3.8.1.en: This verse may seem different from (ch. 1:8), which states that we are sinners. But what is meant is that if we abide in our sonship to God we are averse to sin, yet because of our weakness we fall into it by our own will; the love of God, however, accepts us again through repentance and we regain our sonship in Him.

3.8.2.en: Remember your sonship to God at the beginning of each day, so that it draws you toward Him through prayer and an inclination to do good, and places a barrier between you and sin, however pleasant or tempting it seems.

3.9.0.en: The Apostle gives two marks of the children of God that distinguish them from the children of the devil, which are:

3.9.1.en: 1- Righteousness, that is, purity, holiness and the good life, which we spoke about in detail as the fruit of our sonship to God (vv. 1-9).

3.9.2.en: 2- Love for the brethren as a proof of our love for God and our sonship to Him.

3.10.0.en: The message that you heard from the beginning: The commandment in the Old Testament, "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself" (Lev 19:18), and also the preaching of the Gospel, whose content is love, as Christ proclaimed this same verse mentioned above (Mt 22:39). So St. John affirms that love for the brethren is the proof of our sonship to God, as it came in the proclamation of the Gospel and as the Old Testament also proclaimed.

3.11.1.en: He gives an example of lack of love, which is Cain, who killed his brother Abel, the righteous, who did God's will by offering an animal sacrifice as he had learned from his father Adam, and God accepted it. Cain did not imitate him but was angry with him and his heart was filled with evil, so he killed him to be rid of him. In this it appears that Cain was a son of the wicked Satan by his hatred of his brother.

3.12.0.en: The evil world is subject to its father Satan, so it hates the children of God who are full of love, because their love exposes its evil.

3.13.0.en: Sin, which is selfishness and hatred, has death as its wages, and because of it our first parents were sentenced to death. But when we believed in Christ and received the new nature that leads us to love others, we were freed from eternal death and received the new life in Christ. But whoever persists in not loving others, the sentence of eternal death remains upon him.

3.14.0.en: The beginning of the sin of murder is anger and then hatred, so hatred carries the intention to kill, and whoever persists in hating others condemns himself to perdition and to the loss of his eternity with Christ.

3.15.0.en: Before us is an example of perfect love, which is Christ, who laid down His life for us and died on the Cross. If we believe in His love and redemption we do as He did, being ready to sacrifice even unto death out of our love for others.

3.16.0.en: Whoso hath this world's good: one who has money and possessions beyond his need and can help others with them.

3.16.1.en: He gives an example of love for others, which is a person who has material means that suffice him and more, and God has placed before him a person in need, and he refuses to feel for him and help him. This is contrary to his love for God, because if the love of God were abiding in him he would love his needy brother and help him.

3.16.2.en: Love is the proof of your sonship to God, so may you feel the needs of those around you and help them, especially since their needs may be for kind or encouraging words, a smile, or attentive listening to their troubles, and these things do not cost you much. Why then do you shut up your bowels of compassion toward them, especially since the mercies and benefits of God never leave you?

3.17.0.en: He directs our attention to a third characteristic in addition to purity and love, which is carrying out the commandment in practice, not being content with faith and theoretical conviction, for the demons believe and tremble (Jas 2:19).

3.18.0.en: Practical love confirms that we are children of God, that is, children of the truth, and by this our hearts are made steadfast before Him and we live in assurance.

3.19.1.en: If we examine ourselves and discover the weakness of our love for others, God, who searches the hearts and reins, knows all our weaknesses, accepts our repentance, and helps us to return to Him and to love others.

3.20.0.en: But if our consciences are at rest about our love for others, this gives us assurance and faith to ask for God's grace to be with us so that we grow in this love.

3.21.0.en: God rejoices in the requests of His children who submit to His commandments and do good, and He gives them greater blessings and strength in the growth of their spiritual life and in loving and serving others.

3.22.0.en: St. John sums up the commandments of Christ in two things:

3.22.1.en: 1- Faith in Christ and the love for Him that results from it.

3.22.2.en: 2- Love for others as Christ commanded us often, as in (Jn 13:34).

3.23.0.en: By carrying out the commandment and walking in practical love toward others we abide in God and in His love, and the work of God abides in us. The proof of God's abiding in us is the work of the Holy Spirit, who grants us His fruits such as longsuffering, kindness and love for everyone) .... Gal 5:22.(

3.23.1.en: May your love for others continue even if you are weary or suffering from problems, and however much their demands increase or they wrong you. Do not withhold your love from them or quench the voice of the Holy Spirit within you who calls you to help them.

4.0.0.en: Although St. John is speaking about love, he directs attention to the importance of joining it with discernment, in order to recognize the innovators who creep into the midst of the Church and proclaim ideas strange to it. He calls them false prophets because in pride they think that they are the ones who understand the way of God, and they lead many astray.

4.1.0.en: The Apostle warns against the most important heresy promoted by the innovators, who are antichrists, which is the denial of His divinity and His Incarnation, which is the foundation of the faith. These do not have the Spirit of God but the devil, who resists God. Christ spoke about the appearance of false prophets and antichrists (Mt 24:4, 5). They have appeared since the apostolic age and are still here, proclaiming a new heresy every day, so that outside Egypt there are now hundreds of them, and inside Egypt a new heresy appears every so often, led by one of the servants of the Church, opposing by it the teachings that the Church lives by and has preserved since the days of Christ. Hence we must listen only to the teachers who have the Spirit of God and who believe in the divinity of Christ, His Incarnation, and all the details of faith in Christ that the Church holds to.

4.2.0.en: He encourages his believing children to stand firm in their faith because the Spirit of God is in them, who overcomes Satan and all his ideas which the innovators proclaim. God is stronger than Satan, and however much heresies and heterodoxies increase, He is able to expose their deviation and to triumph over them.

4.3.0.en: The innovators have the evil ideas of the world, so they seek fame, money and the various desires of the world, and everyone who craves these desires is drawn after them, so that they form groups characterized by love of worldly desires.

4.4.0.en: On the other side, the Apostles, among whom is John, have true teachings because they are from God, and everyone who wants to live in purity with God will obey and hold fast to the teachings of the Apostles, which are the teachings of the Church. Thus we distinguish between heresies and sound teachings by submitting to the Church and its teachings, handed down from Christ and the Apostles.

4.4.1.en: Your love for all people does not mean laxity in your faith. Do not listen to any teaching strange to your ears and heart, however dazzling it seems, and hold fast to your Church and its teachings however much the number of innovators grows. Do not doubt your faith because of the wicked boldness of the innovators and their insolence against the Church, which will remain steadfast until the coming of Christ, so that all her children who believe in her may rejoice in eternity.

4.5.0.en: One who is born of God in Baptism receives a new nature inclined to be like God, and then through the Sacrament of the Myron he receives the Holy Spirit and knows God, who is love, and then it is easy for him to love others. Therefore the proof of our love for God is that we love others, and the reverse is true: whoever does not love others, whether by being angry with them, judging them, or wronging them in any way, this is a proof that he does not love God.

4.6.0.en: God revealed love to us by sending His beloved Son to die for us and, by His death, to atone for our sins and take them away from us, so that we may live through Him. There is no greater love than this, that God died for us so that we may live by Him and in Him. God is the one who began the love, not we, but we learn love from Him, and so we love Him because He loved us, gave us life from death, and gave us a new life, which is the life of love.

4.7.0.en: As we respond to God's love for us and love Him, our love for Him results in our loving others, for this is a spontaneous and necessary result.

4.7.1.en: Know that the devil stirs up problems and provokes you with the wrongs of others so that you lose your love toward them, even for moments, and thereby separates you from God, who is true love. So beware of him and be strong by making excuses for others, having compassion on them and loving them for the sake of the One who loved you first, who is God.

4.8.s.en: (3) Abiding in the love of God and its blessings

4.8.0.en: God is an unlimited Spirit, too high for anyone to see Him because of the greatness of His radiance and glory, so no one can see Him, but we can feel Him and behold Him if our hearts are purified from evil and we love one another. The more our love for others increases, the more God abides in us, because His love is perfected in us. As much as we love others we are able to behold God and see Him in us and in those around us.

4.9.0.en: The Holy Spirit who dwells in us is the one who moves us toward loving others, and if we respond to Him God abides in us. Our love for others declares that the Holy Spirit is working in us, and therefore we are abiding in God and submissive to Him.

4.10.0.en: The highest form of love is the love poured out on the Cross for our salvation. This is what the Apostles witnessed and with which they proclaimed the good news to the world.

4.11.0.en: Whoever believes in the incarnate Christ and confesses his faith also believes in God's love poured out on the Cross. God rejoices in him and dwells and abides in him because of his response in faith and love, since his confession is not only theoretical but practical in his life, by loving those around him, and the more he lives by this faith, the more his steadfastness and growth in the knowledge of God increase.

4.12.1.en: As he is, so are we in this world: that is, as Christ lived in the world.

4.12.2.en: A person's abiding in love means his continual growth, and this gives him assurance, so he is not alarmed at the day of judgment but trusts in the forgiving love of Christ, and is encouraged to walk in love with others, following Christ, who loved mankind until He died for it on the Cross.

4.13.0.en: The fear meant is fear of losing material things because of man's attachment to them, as the scholar Tertullian said; whoever loves God is less attached to material things and therefore less fearful of losing them. When love grows and becomes perfect, a person fears nothing in the world, as happened in the lives of the martyrs and saints who sold everything for the love of God.

4.13.1.en: Fear of losing material things results in turmoil in the heart and inner distress, so that a person becomes tormented, wretched and anxious.

4.13.2.en: Fear also means fear of God's punishment for our sins. If a person's love for God becomes perfect, which some saints reach as a very high spiritual degree, like Abba Anthony, father of the monks, then he can be rid of the feeling of fear. But any one of us falls into many sins, and with his love for God, which encourages him to pray and do good, he fears the judgment and hastens to repent. The person remembers that the punishment of his sin is eternal torment, so he fears and returns to God, and this means that he is still liable to fall into sin, that is, that his love is not perfect.

4.14.0.en: God is the source of love for the whole world, and the depth of His love appeared on the Cross in His death for us, and this draws our hearts to Him so that we love Him. Therefore our love for God is a response to His love, because He is the one who began the love, since He came to us by His Incarnation and offered His love on the Cross, and offers it every day on the altar in a broken Body and shed Blood so that we may be saved and live by Him.

4.15.0.en: The Apostle affirms that our love for our brethren is the proof of our love for God, who commanded it (Mt 22:35-39). Then he gives a logical argument to those who claim to love God while they hate their brethren, saying to them: how can you not love your brethren whom you see, though they have virtues, and though you are all human beings, so that you ought to make excuses for one another? It is easier to love those whom you see and to forgive their faults than to claim love for God whom you do not see. This is a higher degree for one who is able to love those he sees and then after that to love the One he does not see, who is God.

4.15.1.en: Be compassionate toward others and forgive quickly if they wrong you, remembering God's forgiveness of you throughout all your past life, knowing that whoever sins is a weak person who needs someone to pray for him and support him with love.

4.15.2.en: Christ guides us to eternal life
